title: C Y P two D six and codeine

segs.text: Section ten. C Y P two D six, debrisoquine, and codeine. Two D six was the first P four fifty enzyme studied in depth and is the best characterized. It metabolizes about fifteen to twenty five percent of the medications on the market.

Debrisoquine is cleared almost entirely by two D six, so grouping people by the ratio of parent drug to metabolite gives a monogenic trait, one gene drives it, and the data separate into distinct peaks for ultrarapid, extensive and poor metabolizers. A smooth bell curve would mean many genes blur the data.

Extra copies of the whole gene, star two times N, make an ultrarapid metabolizer with very fast clearance or activation. Two wild type copies make an extensive, or normal, metabolizer, the common middle. Star five over star five is a whole gene deletion, not an ultrarapid allele, so no enzyme is expressed and the person is a poor metabolizer.

More than one hundred alleles exist, but about nine account for over ninety five percent of phenotypes, in three groups. Star one and star two are fully functional. Star three, four, five and six are nonfunctional. Star ten, seventeen and forty one have reduced function.

For a drug two D six clears, a poor metabolizer accumulates it and has adverse effects at standard doses. For a prodrug it activates, a poor metabolizer makes too little active drug and therapy fails. Codeine is that prodrug: two D six turns it into morphine. An ultrarapid metabolizer turns a normal dose into a large amount of morphine, which can suppress breathing; children died after codeine for cough, so codeine cough syrup is no longer given to kids. A much higher dose can suit an ultrarapid metabolizer on a drug two D six clears, but never on codeine.
